newsitem.title: USA: Productivity revised to rise of 0.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Productivity revised to rise of 0.5 percent.

text.p: U.S. businesses were more efficient in the second quarter of the year than previously estimated, but still lagged their performance of the first quarter, the Labour Department said Tuesday.

Productivity outside of the agricultural sector rose at a seasonally adjusted 0.5 percent annual rate in the second quarter -- instead of falling 0.1 percent -- after growing at a 1.8 percent pace in the first quarter, the department said.

Non-farm productivity provides an assessment of the efficiency of business by measuring the amount of goods and services produced per hour by all workers. Growth in productivity allows wages to rise proportionately without accelerating inflation.

The upward revision, which was slightly higher than Wall Street economists had expected, reflected a much stronger 4.9 percent growth rate in the nation's output than the previously estimated 4.2 percent, the department said.
A slight upward revision in workers' hours to a 4.4 percent growth rate from 4.3 percent also contributed to the higher productivity pace for in the second quarter, it said.

Unit labour costs, which make up two-thirds of businesses' production costs, rose at only a 3.2 percent rate in the second quarter, instead of 3.8 percent, but were still up sharply from the first quarter's tame 1.5 percent growth rate, it said.
Last year productivity rose 0.7 percent after a rise of 0.5 percent in 1994.

Much of the upward revision in second-quarter productivity was focused in the manufacting sector, especially in durable goods producing industries, the department said. Manufacturing includes about 18 percent of the nation's business sector employment.
Manufacturing productivity rose at a 2.2 percent pace in the second quarter -- instead of a 1.5 percent rate -- after a 5.6 percent surge in the first quarter.
